classification.difficultyReason: Prove congruence and identify equal angles at the intersection, including recognising coincident rays in part c, then combine equality with a straight angle to establish perpendicularity.

content.prompt: In each part below, use congruent triangles to prove that the lines $AB$ and $PQ$ are perpendicular. The point $O$ is always the centre of the circle.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle APQ, segment AB to the base, double ticks on AP and AQ, and alpha on both apex angles.
spec.mathematics: AP = AQ; angle PAB = angle BAQ; P,B,Q collinear.

answer.short: $\triangle BAP\equiv\triangle BAQ$ (SAS). Equal adjacent angles $\angle ABP$ and $\angle ABQ$ sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$ and $AB\perp PQ$.
answer.worked:
$AP=AQ$ (given), $AB=AB$ (common side), and $\angle PAB=\angle BAQ=\alpha$ (given).

Therefore $\triangle BAP\equiv\triangle BAQ$ (SAS).

Hence $\angle ABP=\angle ABQ$ (matching angles).

Also $\angle ABP+\angle ABQ=180^\circ$ (straight angle at $B$). Thus both angles are $90^\circ$, so $AB\perp PQ$.

spec.description: Circle centred at O with chord PBQ bisected at B; B,O,A collinear; OP and OQ are drawn.
spec.mathematics: PB = BQ; OP = OQ; OB common.

answer.short: $\triangle OBP\equiv\triangle OBQ$ (SSS). Their equal adjacent angles at $B$ are $90^\circ$, so $AB\perp PQ$.
answer.worked:
$OP=OQ$ (radii), $PB=QB$ (given), and $OB=OB$ (common side).

Therefore $\triangle OBP\equiv\triangle OBQ$ (SSS).

Hence $\angle OBP=\angle OBQ$ (matching angles). Since $P,B,Q$ are collinear, these angles sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$.

Since $B,O,A$ are collinear, $AB\perp PQ$.

spec.description: APB and QVB share vertex B on lines AB and PQ. AP and VQ are 5; PB and VB are 3. Alpha labels APB and BVQ; the latter uses an annotation leader.
spec.mathematics: AP = QV = 5; PB = VB = 3; angle APB = angle QVB = alpha; P,B,Q and A,V,B collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: No right-angle square, calculated length or additional geometric curve.

answer.short: $\triangle APB\equiv\triangle QVB$ (SAS). Thus $\angle ABP=\angle QBV$. They are supplementary, so each is $90^\circ$ and $AB\perp PQ$.
answer.worked:
$AP=QV=5$ and $PB=VB=3$ (given), and $\angle APB=\angle QVB=\alpha$ (given).

Therefore $\triangle APB\equiv\triangle QVB$ (SAS).

Hence $\angle ABP=\angle QBV$ (matching angles). Since rays $BA$ and $BV$ coincide, $\angle QBV=\angle QBA$.

The adjacent angles $\angle ABP$ and $\angle QBA$ sum to $180^\circ$, so each is $90^\circ$. Therefore $AB\perp PQ$.
